name: Cheek dimple device

image.caption: Woman wearing Isabelle Gilbert's Dimple Maker invention

lead: A cheek dimple device is a small mechanism that presses knobs or a brace into the cheeks, intended to form dimples at the smile line. Dimples are widely seen as attractive, so these gadgets were marketed as a way to add them.

The Dolly Dimpler was advertised in Photoplay in 1926, and Isabella Gilbert's Dimple Maker of 1936 was a face-fitting brace with spring-loaded knobs. Surgical dimple creation, a different approach, became available from the 1960s.

paras: Users wore or held the device against the cheeks for periods of time, pressing in at the point where a dimple would appear. The pressure was intended to leave a lasting dent.
It is unknown whether the effect lasted. The American Medical Association reportedly argued frequent users could develop cancer, a claim from period accounts.

lead: Cheek dimple devices are mechanical gadgets sold to press dimples into the cheeks. The Dolly Dimpler was advertised in Photoplay in 1926, and Isabella Gilbert's 1936 Dimple Maker, a face-fitting brace, pushed dents into the cheeks [1][2].

They help looks only as a claimed route: dimples are often considered attractive, and the device aimed to produce them on demand. Natural dimples may arise from variations in the zygomaticus major muscle, such as a double or bifid form, and babies can lose theirs with age [1].
Mental Floss describes Gilbert's device as spring-loaded, pressing two knobs into the cheeks [2].

paras: Wikipedia notes the Dolly Dimpler advertised in 1926 and Isabella Gilbert's 1936 Dimple Maker. It is unknown whether the effect lasted, and the AMA reportedly argued frequent users could develop cancer [1].
Surgical creation became available in the 1960s; Khoo Boo-Chai's 1962 study identified the KBC point where dimples typically form [1].
